MSIB 01-26 - State Highway 35 Bridge - Victoria Barge Canal - Issued: 2026-01-05 --- The U.S. Coast Guard Captain of the Port Corpus Christi has received reports of tug and barge allisions with the State Highway 35 Bridge and its accompanying fendering system near position 28-31-06.48N 096-48-16.92W.  Due to the narrow nature of transiting under the bridge, the U.S. Coast Guard requests all mariners exercise caution when transiting the bridge, utilize side lights and appropriate lookouts for better visibility at night, and report any allisions with the bridge or its fendering immediately to the U.S. Coast Guard.  Vessels can report allisions to the U.S. Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi Command Center at (800) 874-2143.  For non-urgent questions and concerns, mariners may email the U.S. Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi Waterways Management Department at: CCWaterways@uscg.mil.

Houston Ship Channel - Morgans Point - VTS USI Canal/San Jacinto Bay Channel Directive --- The USI Canal/San Jacinto Bay Channel has become increasingly trafficked over the last 2 years.  For various reasons, many tows attempt to reconfigure between Morgans Point and Exxon to go into or come out of the USI Canal.  This practice has resulted in several near miss situations between Morgans Point and the Exxon Terminal in the Houston Ship Channel.  In order to fulfill the VTS mission of reducing risk of collision, allision, damage, pollution, and injury, the following Directive is in effect and will be written as policy in documentation updates to the U.S. Coast Guard VTS Houston-Galveston User Guide: • Vessel Traffic Service Houston-Galveston Directs no barge work in the Houston Ship Channel between Morgans Point and Exxon for purposes of going into/out of the USI Canal. •

--- U.S. Coast Guard Heartland District Hurricane Season 2026 --- The 2026 Hurricane Season extends from June 1, 2026 through November 30, 2026.  Tropical storms and hurricanes often develop with little warning.  Extensive damage to small craft often results in loss of life.  All mariners, particularly operators of small fishing vessels, are reminded that advanced planning, which may prevent loss of vessel and crew, should include:  
a) Instruction of crew and passengers in location of emergency equipment and emergency procedures.
b) Pre-sailing check of vessel, machinery, and equipment for seaworthiness.
c) Installation of strong ground tackle.
d) Review of storm center evacuation procedures.
e) Knowledge of the nearest hurricane shelter or port of refuge.
f) Constant radio watch on VHF-FM Channel 16 and frequent monitoring of VHF-FM Weather Channel for National Weather Service Broadcas

-- MSIB 26-08 Menhaden Season -- This annual MSIB is issued to provide awareness for the Gulf Menhaden seasonal event.  Throughout the Houston Ship Channel, Menhaden have been known to accumulate in sea strainers and cause loss or reduction in propulsion, reduced maneuverability, and loss of water pressure within the firefighting systems.  This is typically a seasonal event primarily occurring in the months of March thru October (although vessels have reported Menhaden impacts year-round).  Menhaden are typically found in coastal and inland tidal waters, and can form large surface schools, appearing in near-shore Gulf waters.  Schools of fish can be drawn into the vessel’s sea chest, clogging the sea strainers, reducing cooling, and causing high water/oil temperatures. Operations will take place in an area bound by approximate positions: 28-03-37.46N 096-58-43.19W, 28-04-59.34N  096-57-37.17W, 28-03-07.75N 096-58-01.02W, 28-03-59.53N  096-57-13.23W.  On-scene vessels will include a push boat, the M/V KEISHA, and the Crew Boats BO26, BO33, and MARINE.  Mariners are urged to transit the area at their slowest safe speed to minimize wake.  VHF-FM Channel: 16, POC: (469) 964-7804

Corpus Christi Channel - Dredge Operation --- From: 2026-08-28 To: 2027-05-01 --- The Dredge LORRAINE HOOKS and attendant plant will be dredging in the Corpus Christi Channel, from Port Aransas to the Corpus Christi Harbor Entrance.  Operations will be conducted 24-hours a day, 7-days a week.  Floating and submerged pipeline connecting and leading to multiple disposal areas will be present in and along the project area.  The dredge requests all vessels requiring the majority of the channel to navigate safely coordinate passing arrangements at least 1-hour in advance.  Mariners are urged to transit the area at their slowest safe speed to minimize wake and proceed with caution.  VHF-FM Channels: 13 and 16, POC: (337) 794-7046 or (229) 254-4900

Arroyo Colorado River - Dredge Operation --- From: 2026-09-04 To: 2027-01-31 --- The Dredge RANGER will conduct dredging operations from the mouth of the Arroyo Colorado River Cutoff Channel to Rio Hondo, approximate Mile 20.0. Dredging will start near the mouth of the river and proceed west towards the Port of Harlingen.  Operation will take place 24-hours a day, 7-days a week.  On-scene vessels and equipment will include approximately 15,000 linear ft of pipe, two supply barges, one anchor barge, one crane barge, a fuel barge, and three tender boats.  The Dredge RANGER requests vessels transiting this stretch of the river coordinate passing arrangements at least 45-minutes in advance.  Mariners are requested to avoid meeting or overtaking in the area and should transit at their slowest safe speed to minimize wake.  VHF-FM Channels; 13 and 16,  POC: (713) 913-7205

GIWW - Dredge Operation --- From: 2026-09-01 To: 2027-02-21 --- The Dredge VANETA MARIE will be working in the GIWW between Mile 490.5, WHL, and Mile 517.5, WHL.  Operations will be conducted 24-hours a day, 7-days a week.  A combination of floating and submerged pipelines will be laid parallel to the waterway, outside of the channel boundaries.  The dredge will operate across the entire channel width in a single pass and will be limited in maneuverability.   Additional on-scene vessels will include the M/Vs ACADIA, SAGUARO, JAY EM and LITTLE BIGHORN.  Four hour closure windows may be required during different phases of the dredge operation.  Tug and barge traffic are requested not to meet or overtake while transitioning through the active dredge site. d: GIWW - Breakwater Construction --- From: 2026-10-05 To: 2026-12-05 --- Breakwater construction will be conducted in the GIWW, between Miles 428.0 and 431.0, WHL.  Work will be conducted from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., daily.  All work and fleeting will take place outside of the channel.  On-scene vessels will include the M/V BILLY GENE and barges.  Mariners are urged to transit the area at their slowest safe speed to minimize wake and proceed with caution.  VHF-FM Channels: 13, 16 and 72, POC: (318) 729-7516

Corpus Christi Channel - Dredge Operation --- From: 2026-09-24 To: 2026-11-01 --- The Dredge GENERAL EISENHOWER will conduct dredging operations in the Corpus Christi Channel from the US Highway 181 Bridge to the Chemical Basin.  Operations will be conducted 24-hours a day, 7-days a week.  Subline will be located within the project limits transporting dredge spoils to the designated placement areas.  Additional on-scene vessels will include the M/Vs IWO JIMA, CORREGIDOR, BATTLE OF THE BULGE and MIDWAY, and the Crew Boat CAPTAIN WALKER.  Mariners are urged to use extreme caution in the area and transit at their slowest safe speed to minimize wake after passing arrangements have been made.  VHF-FM Channels: 13, 16 and 79

La Quinta Channel - Dredge Operation --- From: 2026-09-24 To: 2026-11-01 --- The Dredge GENERAL EISENHOWER will conduct dredging operations in the La Quinta Channel at the San Patricio Basin.  Operations will be conducted 24-hours a day, 7-days a week.  Subline will be located within the project limits transporting dredge spoils to the designated placement areas.  Additional on-scene vessels will include the M/Vs IWO JIMA, CORREGIDOR, BATTLE OF THE BULGE and MIDWAY, and the Crew Boat CAPTAIN WALKER.  Mariners are urged to use extreme caution in the area and transit at their slowest safe speed to minimize wake after passing arrangements have been made.  VHF-FM Channels: 13, 16 and 79

Freeport Entrance Channel - Dredge Operation --- From: 2026-09-29 To: 2026-10-18 --- The Dredge MBI-12 will be conducting dredging operations along the Freeport Entrance Channel at the Freeport LNG Terminal.  Dredged material will be loaded into regulation hopper barges and transported to an unloader barge located at the Freeport LNG Placement Area.  On-scene support vessels will include the T/Vs ADMIRAL, LILY C, WALKER BOONE, CHRISTY C, and ASHLEY ANN.  Mariners are urged to transit at their slowest safe speed to minimize wake and proceed with caution.  VHF-FM Channels: 76 or 78,  POC: (409) 277-5775

Houston Ship Channel - Dredge Operation --- From: 2026-10-14 To: 2026-12-31 --- The Dredge NIMITZ will conduct dredging in the Houston Ship Channel from Houston Ship Channel Lighted Buoy 95 (LLNR-24790.1) to Houston Ship Channel Light 109A (LLNR-25265).  Work will be conducted 24-hours a day, 7-days a week.  The dredge will pump dredged material through pipeline to Alexander Island.  Additional on-scene vessels will include a crane barge, two deck barges, a fuel barge, and the T/Vs MISS PAULA, COURTNEY LUNDIN and KIRA MADISON.  Vessels should coordinate with the dredge at least 45-minutes in advance to ensure equipment can be moved from the channel.  Mariners are urged to transit the area with caution and at their slowest safe speed after passing arrangements have been made.  VHF-FM Channels: 13, 16 and 79, POC: (713) 913-7207
